state.description: Agile boards keyed by zero-padded id; one project per board. Only scrum boards own sprints.
Issue comments keyed `{issueId padded}/{commentId padded}` so one issue's comments scan as a prefix in creation order. Bodies are ADF documents.
Site-wide issue types keyed by id; a project references a creatable subset. hierarchyLevel: -1 subtask, 0 standard, 1 epic.
Issues keyed by zero-padded numeric id. Keys are `<PROJECTKEY>-<n>`; `description` is an ADF document or null; `sprintId` references `sprints`; timestamps are Jira-format strings in UTC.
Id sequences (rowId `counters`): the next issue id and the next comment id. Created lazily when absent.
Priorities keyed by id; lower ids rank higher. Id `3` (Medium) is the default on create.
Project role grants keyed `{projectId padded}/{accountId}`; the project lead is an implicit Administrator.

Projects keyed by zero-padded numeric id. `accessLevel` (open/limited/private) and `project-members` rows decide visibility and write permission; `workflowId` selects the status graph; `issueKeyCounter` is the last issue number handed out.
The single Jira Cloud site (rowId `site`): cloud id, base URL for every `self` link, server title, locale, time zone, default assignee type and the scan bounds (`limits`).
Sprints keyed by zero-padded id, owned by a scrum board. Issues reference a sprint through `sprintId` (rendered as the Sprint custom field customfield_10020).
Statuses keyed by id with their category (2 To Do, 4 In Progress, 3 Done). Names repeat across workflows exactly as in Jira.
Atlassian accounts keyed by accountId. `active: false` accounts and `app` accounts can be referenced by issues but never authenticate or receive assignments.
Status graphs keyed by id: the initial status, the ordered statuses and the transitions (`from: []` means from any status).

connections.title: Atlassian Remote MCP Server Jira tool names (getJiraIssue, searchJiraIssuesUsingJql, ...)
connections.instructions: Connect a Streamable HTTP MCP client to ATLASSIAN_MCP_URL with ATLASSIAN_MCP_TOKEN as a Bearer token. Twelve Jira tool names of the Atlassian Remote MCP Server are exposed as aliases next to the canonical jira.<operation> names; the official hosted server itself is not the client being run.

connections.title: Jira Cloud REST client (base URL + bearer token)
connections.instructions: Point the client at JIRA_BASE_URL and send JIRA_API_TOKEN as `Authorization: Bearer` (the isolated world token; Basic email:token authentication is not accepted). Only the documented route subset exists; every other Jira path answers 404.
